# R269 — native prefill dequant batching: submission, ring lifetime, and safe test bounds

Date: 2026-10-12 (JST). Read-only audit of integrated WN source `0691bcdf5af63a85b3b25650f367d3276db64035`. No model, GPU, CPU test, build, profiler, AST/import, lint, Git, cleanup, or active Main log/receipt action was performed. No source change was made. The recommendations below are source-supported trial conditions, not a run authorization or a performance result.

## Scope, identity, and prior evidence reconciliation

The supplied registry v162 was read at `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/diag-cpu-job-and-raw-bench-20261012/bench/results/2026-10-12-avx2-expert-roofline-and-paired-gu/report-registry-v162.json`, SHA-256 `82e914c8ef9682b1ed870538f8dfa6d8b351a8efb8e54ccc15bb4bdfd046c6a8`, 775 entries. It includes R268’s note that its cache screens do not establish a winner/default or quality equivalence. No R269 result is registered there. R268 is about Prefill scratch retirement/cache growth; its source pin matches this audit’s Prefill file, so it is useful for resource lifetime but does not evaluate the batch call windows.

Source SHA-256 at the requested immutable WN worktree:

- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: `2922806c8b56b64e1bc20096d93c852a105ed225ff3bf9dcf113436c79964d9c`
- `src/kernels/xe/iq_kernels.cpp`: `75f2ac1dfdb337c424bba19e62c34159a1bde547a776b9b5d6cf7975dfc29d50`
- `include/strata/kernels/iq_kernels.hpp`: `61513ccb71831d1065bd25829541c508adf3ae58e1e3df6d3bc0c9681cb54f6d`
- `src/core/gpu.cpp`: read for event submission semantics; source lines below are in the pinned WN tree.
- `src/core/device.cpp`: read to establish stream queue ordering.

R159’s committed seven-pair GPU evidence is directly relevant to the grouped API implementation: all seven active format pairs, 640×2560 matrices, group widths 1/8/16, six ABBA samples per pair/width, and complete output-buffer comparisons; grouped output bytes matched the individual GPU path for those fixtures. Its current IQ kernel source hash is identical to the requested WN source hash. This validates finite grouped-vs-individual GPU output equivalence, including partial widths 1 and 8. It does not validate independent CPU/GPU rounding, current Prefill caller ring ownership, long-context completion, or end-to-end speed.

The old `research-native-batch-compiled-call-path-v1.txt`, R173 service-bound review, and R173 stream-credit/tail review already cover the broad call-path and proposed window histogram. This report narrows them to the requested integrated commit, actual per-flush command count, queue/event ownership, and the 8K/16K effective-ring consequence. Do not re-use the earlier fa3/v6 caller receipts as proof of a batch-on result for this integrated 0691 build. The earlier N64 diagnostic with 144/144 experts resident exercises batch calls on resident pointers, not the streamed copied-slot lifetime. Conversely, older 32K G16 diagnostics used chunk=6144, including a 2047-position tail that routes through the eight-slot non-stream path; they do not qualify 8K/16K all-full-stream chunking.

## What `STRATA_PREFILL_NATIVE_DEQUANT_BATCH=1` selects

`prefill.cpp:2227–2232` enables the branch only when the environment parses nonzero, the layer layout is native, and MMQ is off. The current dequant-to-FP16 APIs are in the fallback product route; the caller continues to use the existing grouped product GEMMs afterward (`2187–2225`, `2478–2503`). `g_expert_group` defaults to 16 and is independently clamped to 1–64 (`191`, `1060`); this group controls expanded-weight destination slots and when the unchanged GEMMs run. The dequant API has its own hard maximum of 16 experts per call (`2242–2260`, `include/strata/kernels/iq_kernels.hpp` group capacity). Each call’s destination is rebased at the group’s current `q` (`2268–2272`) and must be contiguous (`2482–2485`). Therefore `G=16` does not mean the router or all nonresident experts form one single dequant call, and raising `G` cannot raise a call above 16.

At each nonempty `native_flush`, the caller issues one GU group API attempt and one Down group API attempt (`2273–2288`). If admitted, each API submits exactly one `queue.parallel_for`: one GU launch has expert × gate/up parity axes (`iq_kernels.cpp:1724–1748`); one Down launch has an expert axis (`1751–1774`). Hence for the actually accepted grouped path, the emitted dequant kernel count is exactly `GU-admitted + Down-admitted` (one per admitted axis per flush). A declined GU axis launches one old GU kernel for each fallback expert; a declined Down axis launches one old Down kernel per fallback expert. The old GU wrapper uses one parallel_for with the gate/up plane as an axis (`1622–1637`), and the old Down wrapper one flat dequant launch (`1597–1601`). Across a layer/chunk, source counts let Main derive:

`dequant kernel commands = gu_admitted + down_admitted + gu_fallback_experts + down_fallback_experts`.

This formula assumes the source group receipt is complete for that layer/chunk. `flushes` is not itself a launch count because each axis can be declined and fall back. The existing group log (`2575–2583`, emitted when transfer counts are enabled) records admitted/declined attempts and covered/fallback experts by axis. The older `native_dequant_gu_calls/native_dequant_down_calls` census fields increment on per-expert paths/fallbacks (`2277–2287`, `2489–2493`); an accepted grouped launch does not increment those individual-call counters. Do not interpret zero individual-call counters as no batch dequant work. The current aggregate group log does not provide a histogram of `nd_n` per flush or all flush causes; prior R173 already identified this missing width attribution.

`true` from a group API means validated and submitted, not completed. The API validates before submission (`iq_kernels.cpp:1669–1719`); it returns `false` for an axis that fails type/geometry/capacity/alignment/overlap or workgroup-size admission (`1724–1732`, `1751–1759`). GU and Down admission are independent. A GU accepted/Down declined combination is explicitly handled: accepted GU remains queued and the old per-expert Down work is enqueued on the same compute queue before the unchanged products. A submission/execution exception is not converted into the soft `false` path; it propagates into Prefill’s existing error/drain handling.

## G16 versus ring 8/16; what happens when G exceeds ring

These are separate capacities and resource lifetimes:

- `G` determines `dq_gu`/`dq_d` destination allocation and product grouping. For model geometry here each expert has 3,276,800 FP16 GU elements and 1,638,400 FP16 Down elements, or 6,553,600 and 3,276,800 bytes respectively. At G16 that is 157,286,400 bytes (150 MiB) total expanded-weight scratch, independent of staging-ring depth (`prefill.cpp:65–66, 836–837`).
- `m.ring` is source-blob staging/issuer-credit capacity. `STAGE=8`, `STREAM_ALL_MIN=2048`, and `ring_slots(T)` clamps the environment/default value to 16–1024 for large chunks, but returns the fixed 8 for `T<2048` (`69`, `125`, `159–175`). `stream_all` also requires `m.ring>8`, `T>=2048`, and a source (`1390`).
- The dequant window `nd_n` is at most 16. It can be shorter due to the group tail, stream credit, any skipped entry, or a held staging-slot reuse. Full-stream consumer skips call `native_flush` before releasing skipped entries (`2535–2545`). The non-full-stream path flushes before `stage_next` would overwrite a held slot (`2510–2518`). A window width cannot be inferred from either `G` or `ring` alone.

When `G > ring`, the code does not have a special fallback to individual dequant. It flushes bounded contiguous batches as needed, continues at the next contiguous `q` slot, and runs the original grouped GEMMs when the existing G-group is complete or at its tail (`2242–2272`, `2481–2503`). The separate per-expert fallback happens only when a specific grouped API axis declines. With full-stream ring16 and G64, four 16-entry dequant windows can fill the four contiguous portions of the G64 expanded-weight buffer before the unchanged products; source credits are returned after each flush. With ring8 non-stream mode, the STAGE reuse collision can force earlier flushes. In both cases flushes keep the input blobs alive until their grouped GU and Down readers have been enqueued behind the copy-completion dependency and the used-slot event is recorded after those readers.

The `G16/ring16` numerical equality is coincidental: two independent ceilings happen to share the number 16. Even when ring16 and G16 match, routing skips and resident experts can shorten the native window. Conversely a larger ring does not raise the 16 expert API cap or widen the G16 GEMM group.

### Effective ring for requested chunk sizes

For 8K and 16K chunks (`T=8192`/`16384`), `T >= 2048`. `STRATA_PREFILL_RING=8` is clamped to effective `m.ring=16`; setting it to 16 produces the same capacity. Thus an environment-only “ring 8 vs 16” comparison at 8K/16K is not a real treatment. To compare effective 8 with 16 at all, a source change would have to lower the minimum clamp for `T>=2048`; that would alter producer-credit behavior and is not warranted before the current instrumentation/reuse protocol is separately qualified. Do not make this source change as the first trial.

At `T<2048`, ring remains 8 regardless of the environment override and the route uses the ordinary stage-next consumer rather than the full-stream sequence. The old N64 test setting `ring=8` is therefore the expected small-chunk route, but its all-resident profile does not exercise the staging events. At 8K/16K, explicitly set `STRATA_PREFILL_RING=16` and capture the effective ring in the launch receipt; this removes dependence on the default ring auto-sizing and avoids claiming an untested eight-slot full-stream case. `ring=32` is a distinct possible future producer-credit experiment, but earlier R173 source review already concludes it cannot increase `nd_n` above 16; it is not a first-line dequant-batch setting.

## Input/output event ownership and retirement

`Runtime` creates both compute and transfer queues as SYCL `in_order` queues and creates engine streams the same way (`src/core/device.cpp:185–187, 223–226`). The grouped API uses `queue_for(stream)` (`iq_kernels.cpp:61–67`); with `m.cs`, grouped GU, grouped Down, old-axis fallback, the `event_record(m.used[slot], m.cs)`, and later GEMM submissions are ordered on that compute queue.

The full-stream producer writes a source blob to `stage_dev[sl]` on `m.copy`, records that completion as `m.copied[sl]` (`gpu.cpp:242–250`), and the consumer makes `m.cs` wait for `m.copied[sl]` before reading the blob (`prefill.cpp:2551–2562`). `copy_async_after` binds the current slot’s previous-reader event in the copy submission’s dependency list (`gpu.cpp:242–249`); in-order transfer submission then protects stage-slot overwrite. In batch mode, the consumer retains each streamed blob in `nd_blob[]`/`nd_slot[]` until `native_flush` has submitted both dequant readers. Only then does it record `m.used[sl]` on compute for each held stream slot and advance `consumed`/give the producer its credit (`2289–2299`). This is the key source ownership invariant: `used` closes after *both* readers, not after the first axis and not merely after the host copies the pointers.

The grouped API copies the pointer table and scalar fields into a local `IqDequantGroup` value before submitting its kernel (`iq_kernels.cpp:1733–1737, 1760–1764`). The closure uses those copied pointer values. Therefore the stack `ng` table may retire after API submission, but every `nd_blob[i]` underlying allocation/slot must remain valid until its recorded used event. The group output addresses refer into Prefill-owned `m.dq_gu`/`m.dq_d`, whose slots remain live through the unchanged grouped GEMMs; same in-order `m.cs` queue ordering places product reads after dequant writes and any next dequant reuse after the earlier product. It is not safe to reuse a q slot merely because the host API returned.

The Prefill chunk state includes the stager and sequence, events, buffers, and ring. The completion guards cancel/join the stager and drain both compute/copy queues before chunk storage retires (`1434–1454`, `1497–1509`, `2584`; in unwind, see the destructors around `1434–1453` and `1497–1508`). At Prefill object retirement, `release()` drains compute and copy before resetting stager/freeing buffers and destroying the ring events (`prefill.cpp:539–556`). This aligns with R268: do not reset/rebuild/release Prefill scratch while either queue or producer can still read it.

Potential lifetime fix: none identified for the reviewed native-batch path. The current slot event is recorded after both grouped/fallback consumers and producer credit follows it. This audit does not prove backend correctness for every failure mode or every runtime; preserve checked queue drains and exercise normal/error paths when Main qualifies the path. Do not remove/add volatile sharing, event reuse, or early `consumed` publication.

## Existing numeric evidence: what it closes and what remains open

- **R159 component evidence:** seven active type pairs, 640×2560, grouped widths 1/8/16, full GPU output bytes equal to individual GPU output on tested inputs; six ABBA samples per pair/width. This supports kernel-level parity on those shapes, including non-full groups.
- **Small model diagnostic:** the earlier 64-token OFF/ON test completed with the same 16 generated IDs/T/LP5 records and strict health. Its receipt also says 144/144 profile experts resident, so it is not a streamed-source ring-lifetime test. It is diagnostic only, not 262144-context qualification or performance eligibility.
- **Earlier 32K diagnostic:** it used G16 and requested ring8, but source-clamped effective full-stream ring to16 for 6144-token chunks; its final 2047-position chunk used the STAGE8 non-stream path. It is not a literal full-stream ring8 comparison and it predates this exact integrated source identity in the cited v6 evidence.

No existing evidence read here establishes an end-to-end improvement, a no-hang guarantee, a complete 8K/16K stream-lifetime pass, all-output precision against an independent oracle, or full 262144-position context qualification.

## Narrow, low-risk qualification sequence

Keep physical context/capacity at 262144 and keep `G=16`; do not alter ring clamp, reorder routes, or change dequant arithmetic. Start with the current existing path only: paired `STRATA_PREFILL_NATIVE_DEQUANT_BATCH=0` and `=1`, with all other binary/source/runtime/input/settings fixed, explicit `STRATA_PREFILL_RING=16`, and `--prefill 8192` for a 32K prompt. At 8K chunks this is four chunks; every chunk remains at least 2048, so the source stays in the full-stream branch and the effective ring is 16. Use Main’s existing READY memory admission gate and all existing source/build/provider/health/fault gates. Before treating ON as submitted, reconcile each per-layer/chunk group receipt with transfer/route evidence, including each axis’ admitted/declined and covered/fallback experts. Then compare all generated IDs, per-token `T` and LP5 evidence, normal completion/QUIT, and repeated quiet endpoint prefill times. Keep diagnostic census output separate from quiet timings.

If both arms close without new faults and route/order counts match, use the same controlled pair at `--prefill 16384` for a 64K prompt (four chunks), again keeping context=262144, G16, effective ring16, and only the batch environment variable changed between OFF and ON. Compare 64K and 32K separately; don't pool samples across chunk sizes. This ensures the actual branch and T-sized chunks are tested while retaining the full configured capacity. A later true full-context request still needs its own completion/quality evidence; 262144 capacity on a 32K/64K request must not be reported as full-context qualification.

For a diagnostic-only first pair, enable the already-existing transfer/group receipt and capture the effective ring/chunk size. The group receipt already gives enough aggregate counts to reconstruct submitted grouped/fallback launch count using the formula above. If a performance attribution is needed, the minimal additional source candidate is a fixed 17-bin `nd_n=0..16` flush histogram plus a small per-layer effective-ring value (and, only if it changes the interpretation, reason counters for stream-credit, skip, non-stream held reuse, G-tail, and 16-entry cap). Emit aggregates once per layer/chunk, without per-expert output, extra stream sync, wait, or timestamp event. Separate this diagnostic arm from quiet timings. R173 already proposed the width/reason census; no need to repeat it unless the current integrated receipts still lack it.

For precision/order gates, preserve the existing product path and route order byte-for-byte; compare all generated outputs on deterministic matched requests and retain full per-token IDs/T/LP5, not just final text. R159 grouped-vs-individual device output parity is a prerequisite, not a substitute for these model comparisons or an independent half-conversion oracle. For safety, require normal checked drain at every request/chunk close, no warning/fault/nonfinite/truncation, and do not accept `API returned true` as completion proof.

No code-level ring or event fix is justified from this source review alone. If a later receipt shows slot-credit wait or short `nd_n` windows dominate, the first source change should be the bounded diagnostic above, not moving the `used` event earlier or changing the full-stream protocol. If the API admits the group but a stream never drains, stop the batch-on arm and preserve the representative fault receipt; don't disable drains or fall through as if the queue had completed.

## Primary references

- [Khronos SYCL 2020 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html) and [SYCL reference for command-group dependencies](https://github.khronos.org/SYCL_Reference/iface/command-group-handler.html): command submission/dependency semantics. They support event-edge reasoning, not a guarantee about a particular Level Zero driver’s progress or latency.
- [Intel oneAPI SYCL graph usage guide](https://intel.github.io/llvm/syclgraph/SYCLGraphUsageGuide.html): Intel examples use in-order queue ordering and explicit event dependencies to keep an allocation alive through its last consumer. This is analogous ownership context, not a Strata-specific qualification.
- [ggml SYCL conversion source](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/convert.cpp): primary adjacent implementation showing SYCL `parallel_for` dequantization launches. It is not Strata’s group API, source lifetime scheme, or performance evidence.
